b:
A tool whose rules, when observed, protect the mind from error in thinking. It is a practical science that serves other sciences, as grammar serves the tongue.

al-Jurjani, al-Ta'rifat: «المنطق: آلة قانونية تعصم مراعاتها الذهن عن الخطأ في الفكر»

f: Why do the scholars study mantiq before the higher texts?
b: Because kalam, usul al-fiqh and balaghah are written in its terms: definitions, propositions and syllogisms. Without it a student cannot follow their arguments.

f: What is fikr (thinking), in the terms of logic?
b:
Arranging things already known so as to reach something unknown.

al-Jurjani, al-Ta'rifat: «الفكر: ترتيب أمور معلومة للتأدي إلى مجهول»

f: Into which two kinds is knowledge divided?
b: Tasawwur (conception): grasping a thing without judging anything about it; and tasdiq (assent): judging that something is or is not so.

The presence of a thing's form in the mind.

al-Jurjani, al-Ta'rifat: «التصور: حصول صورة الشيء في العقل»

f: What is the difference between badihi and nazari knowledge?
b:
Badihi (self-evident) knowledge comes without reflection or effort; nazari (acquired) knowledge needs reflection and effort to reach.

al-Jurjani, al-Ta'rifat: «النظري: هو الذي يتوقف حصوله على نظر وكسب»

f: Give al-Jurjani's examples of nazari knowledge.
b:
Conceiving the soul and the intellect, and assenting that the world is originated.

al-Jurjani, al-Ta'rifat: «كتصور النفس والعقل، وكالتصديق بأن العالم حادث»

f: What leads to a conception, and what leads to an assent?
b: A definition (qawl sharih) leads to a conception; a proof (hujjah) leads to an assent.

A thing being such that knowing it requires knowing something else. The first is the dall (signifier), the second the madlul (signified).

al-Jurjani, al-Ta'rifat: «الدلالة: هي كون الشيء بحالة يلزم من العلم به العلم بشيء آخر»

f: What are the three kinds of verbal signification?
b: Mutabaqah: a word signifies its whole meaning ("house" for the whole house). Tadammun: it signifies part of its meaning ("house" for the roof). Iltizam: it signifies something outside its meaning that is necessarily tied to it ("house" for the builder).

A meaning whose very conception does not prevent it being shared by many, like "human".

al-Jurjani, al-Ta'rifat: «ما لا يمنع نفس تصوره من وقوع الشركة فيه، كالإنسان»

A meaning whose very conception prevents it being shared, like Zayd.

al-Jurjani, al-Ta'rifat: «ما يمنع نفس تصوره من وقوع الشركة، كزيد»

f: What are the five universals (al-kulliyyat al-khams)?
b: Genus (jins), species (naw'), differentia (fasl), property (khassah) and general accident ('arad 'amm). The first three are essential; the last two are accidental.

A name that applies to many things differing in species, like "animal".

al-Jurjani, al-Ta'rifat: «الجنس: اسم دال على كثيرين مختلفين بالأنواع»

A name that applies to many things differing only as individuals, like "human".

al-Jurjani, al-Ta'rifat: «النوع: اسم دال على أشياء كثيرة مختلفة بالأشخاص»

A universal said of a thing in answer to "which thing is it, in its essence?", like "rational" for the human.

al-Jurjani, al-Ta'rifat: «الفصل: كلي يحمل على الشيء في جواب أي شيء هو في جوهره، كالناطق والحساس»

A universal said accidentally of the members of one reality only, like "able to write" for the human.

al-Jurjani, al-Ta'rifat: «الخاصة: كلية مقولة على أفراد حقيقة واحدة فقط قولا عرضيا»

A universal said accidentally of the members of one reality and of others too, like "walking" for the human.

al-Jurjani, al-Ta'rifat: «العرض العام: كلي معقول على أفراد حقيقة واحدة وغيرها قولا عرضيا»

One that applies equally to all its members, like "human".

al-Jurjani, al-Ta'rifat: «المتواطئ: هو الكلي الذي يكون حصول معناه وصدقه على أفراده الذهنية والخارجية على السوية»

f: What is a mushakkik universal? Give al-Jurjani's example.
b:
One that does not apply equally to all its members, being prior, stronger or more fitting in some. His example is existence, which belongs to the Necessary more fittingly, more anciently and more strongly than to the contingent.

al-Jurjani, al-Ta'rifat: «المشكك: هو الكلي الذي لم يتساو صدقه على أفراده»

A word laid down for several meanings by several acts of coinage, like 'ayn (eye, spring, spy).

al-Jurjani, al-Ta'rifat: «المشترك: ما وضع لمعنى كثير بوضع كثير، كالعين»

Words with one meaning and many names, like layth and asad (lion).

al-Jurjani, al-Ta'rifat: «المترادف: ما كان معناه واحدا وأسماؤه كثيرة»

f: What is a hadd (definition) in logic?
b:
A statement that signifies the quiddity (essence) of a thing.

al-Jurjani, al-Ta'rifat: «الحد: قول دال على ماهية الشيء»

f: What is a hadd tamm (complete definition)? Give the example.
b:
One made of the proximate genus and the proximate differentia: "the human is a rational animal".

al-Jurjani, al-Ta'rifat: «الحد التام: ما يتركب من الجنس والفصل القريبين، كتعريف الإنسان بالحيوان الناطق»

f: What is a hadd naqis (incomplete definition)?
b:
One made of the proximate differentia alone, or with a remote genus: "rational", or "a rational body".

al-Jurjani, al-Ta'rifat: «الحد الناقص: ما يكون بالفصل القريب وحده، أو به وبالجنس البعيد»

f: What is a rasm tamm (complete description)?
b:
One made of the proximate genus and a property: "the human is an animal that laughs".

al-Jurjani, al-Ta'rifat: «الرسم التام: ما يتركب من الجنس القريب والخاصة، كتعريف الإنسان بالحيوان الضاحك»

f: What is a rasm naqis (incomplete description)?
b:
One made of a property alone, or with a remote genus: "that which laughs".

al-Jurjani, al-Ta'rifat: «الرسم الناقص: ما يكون بالخاصة وحدها، أو بها وبالجنس البعيد»

f: What is daur (circularity), and why does it spoil a definition or proof?
b:
A thing depending on what depends on it. If A needs B and B needs A, neither is ever reached, so a definition or proof built on it fails.

al-Jurjani, al-Ta'rifat: «الدور: هو توقف الشيء على ما يتوقف عليه»

A statement of which it can be said that the one saying it speaks truly or falsely.

al-Jurjani, al-Ta'rifat: «القضية: قول يصح أن يقال لقائله: إنه صادق فيه أو كاذب فيه»

f: What are the two parts of a categorical (hamliyyah) proposition?
b: The mawdu' (subject), about which the judgement is made, and the mahmul (predicate), which is judged of it. In "Zayd is standing", Zayd is the subject and standing the predicate.

Ijab (affirmation) is establishing the relation between subject and predicate; salb (negation) is removing it.

al-Jurjani, al-Ta'rifat: «الإيجاب: هو إيقاع النسبة»

f: What is the sur of a proposition?
b:
The word that shows the quantity of the subject's members: "every" and "some" in affirmation, "no" and "not every" in negation.

al-Jurjani, al-Ta'rifat: «السور في القضية: هو اللفظ الدال على كمية أفراد الموضوع»
Universal affirmative (every human is an animal); particular affirmative (some animals are human); universal negative (no human is a stone); particular negative (not every animal is human).

One made of two propositions joined together.

al-Jurjani, al-Ta'rifat: «الشرطية: ما تتركب من قضيتين»

One that judges one proposition true on the supposition of another: "if this is a human, it is an animal".

al-Jurjani, al-Ta'rifat: «المتصلة: هي التي يحكم فيها بصدق قضية أو لا صدقها على تقدير أخرى»

One that judges two propositions to be incompatible: "a number is either even or odd".

al-Jurjani, al-Ta'rifat: «المنفصلة: هي التي يحكم فيها بالتنافي بين القضيتين»

Two propositions differing in affirmation and negation so that, by themselves, one must be true and the other false: "Zayd is a human", "Zayd is not a human".

al-Jurjani, al-Ta'rifat: «التناقض: هو اختلاف القضيتين بالإيجاب والسلب، بحيث يقتضي لذاته صدق إحداهما وكذب الأخرى»

f: What is the contradictory of "every human is an animal"?
b: "Not every human is an animal" (a particular negative). The contradictory of a universal is a particular of the opposite quality.

Making the first part of the proposition second and the second first, while its truth and quality stay as they were: "every human is an animal" converts to "some animals are human".

al-Jurjani, al-Ta'rifat: «العكس المستوي: هو عبارة عن جعل الجزء الأول من القضية ثانيا، والجزء الثاني أولا، مع بقاء الصدق والكيف بحالهما»

Putting the contradictory of the second part first and the contradictory of the first part second: "every human is an animal" becomes "whatever is not an animal is not a human".

al-Jurjani, al-Ta'rifat: «عكس النقيض: هو جعل نقيض الجزء الثاني جزءا أولا، ونقيض الأول ثانيا مع بقاء الكيف والصدق بحالهما»

A statement made of propositions which, if granted, necessarily yield another statement by themselves: "the world changes; everything that changes is originated", so "the world is originated".

al-Jurjani, al-Ta'rifat: «القياس: قول مؤلف من قضايا إذا سلمت لزم عنها لذاتها قول آخر»

f: What are the minor term, the major term and the middle term?
b: In "the world changes; everything that changes is originated; so the world is originated": the minor term is "the world" (subject of the conclusion), the major term is "originated" (its predicate), and the middle term is "changes", which joins them and drops out of the conclusion.

f: What is the difference between a qiyas iqtirani and a qiyas istithna'i?
b:
In an istithna'i syllogism the conclusion or its contradictory is stated in the premises ("if this is a body it occupies space; but it is a body"). In an iqtirani syllogism it is not ("the body is composite; every composite is originated").

al-Jurjani, al-Ta'rifat: «القياس الاستثنائي: ما يكون عين النتيجة أو نقيضها مذكورا فيه بالفعل»

f: What is the first figure, and its two conditions?
b: The figure where the middle term is the predicate of the minor premise and the subject of the major. It is the clearest. To produce a conclusion the minor premise must be affirmative and the major universal.

f: How do the four figures differ?
b: By the place of the middle term: (1) predicate of the minor, subject of the major; (2) predicate of both; (3) subject of both; (4) subject of the minor, predicate of the major.

Judging a universal by what is found in most of its particulars. Its premises come only from going through the particulars.

al-Jurjani, al-Ta'rifat: «الاستقراء: هو الحكم على كلي بوجوده في أكثر جزئياته»

f: What is tamthil (analogy), and what do the jurists call it?
b:
Establishing a ruling in one particular because it holds in another, for a meaning they share. The jurists call it qiyas: the first is the far' (branch), the second the asl (root), and the shared meaning the 'illah.

al-Jurjani, al-Ta'rifat: «والفقهاء يسمونه قياسا، والجزئي الأول فرعا والثاني أصلا»

A syllogism made of certain premises, whether self-evident or proven. It is the only argument that yields certainty.

al-Jurjani, al-Ta'rifat: «البرهان: هو القياس المؤلف من اليقينيات»

f: What is jadal (dialectic), and what is it for?
b:
A syllogism made of well-known and accepted premises, used to bind an opponent and silence one unable to grasp a demonstration.

al-Jurjani, al-Ta'rifat: «الجدل: هو القياس المؤلف من المشهورات والمسلمات، والغرض منه إلزام الخصم»

An argument from accepted or probable premises, from someone trusted, to move people to what benefits them, as preachers do.

al-Jurjani, al-Ta'rifat: «الخطابة: هو قياس مركب من مقدمات مقبولة، أو مظنونة»

A corrupt syllogism, faulty either in its form or in its matter.

al-Jurjani, al-Ta'rifat: «المغالطة: قياس فاسد إما من جهة الصورة، أو من جهة المادة»

An argument built from mere fancies, meant to mislead the opponent.

al-Jurjani, al-Ta'rifat: «السفسطة: قياس مركب من الوهميات، والغرض منه تغليط الخصم»

f: What is yaqin (certainty) in the terms of the scholars?
b:
Believing a thing is so, while believing it cannot be otherwise, in agreement with reality, and not liable to disappear.

al-Jurjani, al-Ta'rifat: «اعتقاد الشيء بأنه كذا مع اعتقاد أنه لا يمكن إلا كذا، مطابقا للواقع غير ممكن الزوال»

The preponderant belief, while the opposite remains possible.

al-Jurjani, al-Ta'rifat: «الظن: هو الاعتقاد الراجح مع احتمال النقيض»
